Shop Storefront Brief · Issue 4

Apple published the Creative Assets rulebook on Aug 5. Your 17+ game still markets at 4+.

2026-08-25 · Fortune Insight, LLC · Operator intel for indie iOS teams. This page covers new App Store marketing surfaces and Connect analytics — not a commission or IAP rate change. If you only track fee worksheets, Connect rules did not change because of this news.

What happened

On 2026-08-05 Apple published App Store asset best practices and design templates (Figma, Photoshop, Pixelmator) ahead of a fall launch with iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. The new Creative Assets format sits beside screenshots and app previews: brand headers, seasonal art, and content promos that can appear in the product page header, search results, In-App Events, custom product pages, and Apple Ads placements.

Submission can ride along with an app version or go through the new Asset Library in App Store Connect — upload and review standalone, then deploy approved assets without another app binary. The App Store Connect API supports uploads. A product page preview tool also ships this fall so you can render header + search creative before anything goes live.

Creative Assets rules indie teams should read now

Summary of Apple's published best practices. Final App Review interpretation will happen case by case once submissions open — this note is not legal advice.

Rule area What Apple published
Storefront age ceiling Assets shown on the App Store must meet a 4+ rating — even when your app's own rating is higher (e.g. 12+ or 17+)
Banned in creative assets Specific prices, discounts, URLs, unverifiable awards, other-platform logos, and reproductions of Apple editorial badges (App of the Day, Editor's Choice, etc.)
Video behaviour Autoplay + loop in most placements; audio muted by default — design for silent-first playback
Search results slot Optional custom image/video before the product page; if omitted, Connect falls back to In-App Events, app previews, or screenshots
Asset Library workflow Approved assets can be reused across header and search placements without a second review; seasonal swaps can publish without a new app version

Connect keyword analytics (live since 2026-07-01)

Separate from Creative Assets, App Store Connect now reports per-keyword performance for your own app: impressions, tap-through rate, conversion rate, 1/7/30-day retention cohorts, and attributed IAP revenue by acquisition keyword. Data appears in the Connect web dashboard, the Connect app, and the Analytics Reports API.

Operator catches: you still cannot see competitor keyword stats; retention and revenue lines often lag 5–7 days; API access may require an Account Holder or Admin role. Market-wide demand signals remain the monthly Search Term Rank report and Apple Ads popularity scores — not absolute search volume counts.

What this is not

  • Not a new US or EU commission rate. EU unified terms still land 2026-10-01 — see Issue 0.
  • Not Brazil alternative-distribution math — see Issue 3.
  • Not a guarantee that Creative Assets will rank you higher. They add surfaces; keyword metadata and product quality still drive discovery.
  • If you only sell US IAP inside the App Store and do not run subscriptions: no need to reprice checkout this week because of Creative Assets headlines.

What an indie can do this week

  • Download Apple's Figma/Photoshop/Pixelmator templates and sketch one header + one search asset that survives the 4+ ceiling — no price callouts, no award badges you cannot verify.
  • If you run EU storefronts: confirm whether your Account Holder signed the updated ADPLA before the 2026-10-01 switch — fee math is unchanged from Issue 0, but unsigned accounts may be blocked from new EU payment options.
  • Open Connect → Analytics → filter App Store search keywords for your app; export the top 10 terms by impressions and check whether conversion or 7-day retention justifies keeping them in your 100-character keyword field.
  • Do not rebuild checkout or reprice IAP because of Creative Assets news — this is a marketing-surface change, not a commission update.
